subject: Initial DPA request and subprocessor/transfer questions — FinApp
messages:
From: Jamie Ellis <jamie@finapp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finapp.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA request & subprocessors — FinApp/Redwood

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick intro on the call earlier. FinApp's legal team asked me to follow up with a few items we need to get started on contracting:

- Our procurement/legal team needs a copy of Redwood's standard DPA (we prefer a PDF and any Word redlineable version).
- A current list of subprocessors (processors that may handle customer data), with regions where they operate.
- Confirmation of cross-border transfer approach: do you rely on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), an EU Transfer Addendum, or something else?
- Any account-level data residency options (if we pin to EU regions).
- E-sign preference: does Redwood execute via DocuSign or AdobeSign? We need to open the DocuSign envelope from our side if possible.

If you can send the DPA and subprocessor list today that would keep our procurement timeline moving. We also have a few preliminary redline asks from security about retention/audit logs — I can send those after we get your template.

Best,
Jamie
Jamie Ellis
Head of Legal Ops | FinApp
jamie@finapp.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ellis <jamie@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request & subprocessors — FinApp/Redwood

Hi Jamie — thanks, and great chatting earlier.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf (canonical DPA) and Subprocessor_List_2025-10-02.csv. The CSV includes subprocessor name, function, and primary region. A few quick answers up front:

- Transfers: Redwood relies on the EU SCCs as implemented in our DPA and we can append an EU Transfer Addendum upon request. For customers who require EU-only hosting we can discuss Dedicated/Private deployment options.
- E-sign: we routinely execute DPAs via DocuSign and Adobe Sign; DocuSign is preferred for speed but either works. We can also accept a signed PDF returned by procurement if needed.
- Subprocessor mapping: we provide an account-scoped map (which subprocessors touched tokens for a customer) during onboarding for Dedicated/reserved customers; for Hosted API customers we provide the public subprocessor list and can provide scoped mappings under an enterprise support request.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached DPA and send any redlines (Word or Docx preferred).
2) Karthik (cc'd) will handle security questions and follow up on retention/SOC 2 artifacts.
3) If redlines are minimal we can sign via DocuSign within 48 hours.

We'd like to confirm the target sign-by date for your procurement cycle — is 10/20 workable?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf (69KB), Subprocessor_List_2025-10-02.csv (7KB)

From: Jamie Ellis <jamie@finapp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finapp.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request & subprocessors — FinApp/Redwood

Thanks Vivek — received the PDF and subprocessor list. A few immediate redline asks from our side (attached as FinApp_DPA_Redlines.docx):

- Retention / logs: request that audit logs relevant to API access and administrative actions be retained for at least 12 months; security wants an SLA around providing logs on request (48–72 hours).
- Data deletion: we prefer a 30-day maximum for Redwood to confirm deletion of customer-supplied data on hosted environments after a termination request.
- Transfers: we'd like the DPA to explicitly state that SCCs apply and that Redwood will promptly execute any customer-approved transfer addendum.
- Subprocessor disclosure: legal asks for a clause that Redwood will provide customer-specific subprocessor mapping within 10 business days upon request.

Could you confirm which of these are standard vs. will need commercial discussion? We're OK with DocuSign for final execution — I can open the envelope once we have agreed text.

Jamie

Attachments: FinApp_DPA_Redlines.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ellis <jamie@finapp.com>, Legal Ops <legal@finapp.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request & subprocessors — FinApp/Redwood

Hi Jamie — looping in a few folks from product and security to respond to the redlines. Answers below map to the numbered asks in your docx:

1) Audit logs / retention: our standard retention for API access and admin logs is 12 months; we can commit to supplying relevant logs within 72 hours for hosted customers. If you need a shorter SLA or longer retention we'll treat that as an addendum (common for enterprise customers).

2) Data deletion: for Hosted API we will confirm deletion of customer-supplied data within 30 days of a verified deletion request. Note: model weights / public model caching are separate and not customer-specific. For Dedicated/Private deployments FinApp can control data deletion directly (we'll document the process).

3) Transfers / SCCs: Vivek is correct — the DPA references SCCs. We can add an explicit statement that Redwood will execute an EU Transfer Addendum on request. We'll include language allowing customers to attach a pre-approved transfer addendum.

4) Subprocessor mapping: our public subprocessor list is attached (csv). For account-scoped mappings we will provide a consolidated export for FinApp within 10 business days of a written request — that export will indicate which subprocessors processed requests for your account during a specified period. For any requests that require deeper forensic access (per-request traces) we'll need to scope a support engagement.

5) Execution path: we are happy to use DocuSign (preferred) or Adobe Sign. If you prefer we can prepare the envelope and send to your Legal Ops address.

Next steps:
- If you confirm the redlines that are must-haves vs. negotiable, we'll prepare a tracked redline back with proposed language.
- Vivek / Karthik: please attach SOC 2 summary and the EU transfer addendum draft for Jamie's review.

Thanks and happy to sync live if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
